text:
Predicates:
PerformsOften(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
Attends(x) ::: x attends school events.
Engaged(x) ::: x is very engaged with school events.
CommunityMember(x) ::: x is a member of the community.
InactiveMember(x) ::: x is inactive and disinterested.
Chaperones(x, y) ::: x chaperones y.
HighSchoolDance(y) ::: y is a high school dance.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
WishToAdvance(x) ::: x wishes to further her academic career and educational opportunities.
YoungChildOrTeen(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.
Bonnie ::: Bonnie.
Perform(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows.
Attend(x) ::: x attends school.
Interested(x) ::: x is interested in educational opportunities.
Wishes(x) ::: x wishes to further her career and opportunities.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsOften(x) → Attends(x) ∧ Engaged(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.
∀x (PerformsOften(x) ∨ (InactiveMember(x) ∧ ¬Interested(x))) ::: People either perform often or are inactive and disinterested.
∀x (Chaperones(x, y) ∧ HighSchoolDance(y) → ¬Attend(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend.
∀x (InactiveMember(x) ∧ CommunityMember(x) → Chaperones(x, y) ∧ HighSchoolDance(y)) ::: All inactive members chaperone high school dances.
∀x (YoungChildOrTeen(x) ∧ WishToAdvance(x) → Student(x) ∧ Attend(x)) ::: Young children and teenagers who wish to further their career attend school.
Bonnie ::: Bonnie.
(Attend(Bonnie) ∧ Engaged(Bonnie) ∧ Student(Bonnie)) ∨ (¬Attend(Bonnie) ∧ ¬Engaged(Bonnie) ∧ ¬Student(Bonnie)) ::: Bonnie either attends and is engaged, and is a student, or neither.

Conclusion:
(ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(Bonnie) ∨ (¬ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(Bonnie) ∧ PerformsOften(Bonnie))) → (YoungChildOrTeen(Bonnie) ∧ Wishes(Bonnie) ∧ InactiveMember(Bonnie))
